skill_drafts.name: AgentOps SDK Module Initialization
skill_drafts.description: Initialize and configure the AgentOps SDK by importing core tracing decorators, semantic conventions, and client infrastructure. Establishes the public API surface for agent instrumentation and tracing context setup.
skill_drafts.objective: Set up AgentOps tracing infrastructure and expose public API for agent instrumentation
applicable_signals: Need to access decorators or session management
contraindications: Already in an active tracing session (re-initialization may cause conflicts)
Only legacy session management is required without modern decorator support
workflow_steps: Import legacy session management and event types from agentops.legacy
Import semantic convention classes (AgentAttributes, ToolAttributes, WorkflowAttributes, CoreAttributes, SpanKind, SpanAttributes)
Import TraceContext and tracer from agentops.sdk.core
Re-export all imported items at module level for public API access
triggers: Onboarding AgentOps into an existing codebase
constraints: Must import from agentops.legacy for backward compatibility
Must expose all decorator types (trace, session, agent, task, workflow, operation, tool, guardrail, track_endpoint)
Must include semantic convention attributes and SpanKind enums
Must provide TraceContext and tracer for modern instrumentation
cautions: Ensure OpenTelemetry dependencies are installed before importing trace utilities
Legacy imports must remain available for backward compatibility with existing code
Deprecation warnings should be logged for legacy APIs to guide users toward modern decorators
output_contract: All core decorators (trace, session, agent, task, workflow, operation, tool, guardrail, track_endpoint), semantic attributes (AgentAttributes, ToolAttributes, WorkflowAttributes, CoreAttributes, SpanAttributes, SpanKind), Client, TraceContext, tracer, legacy session management functions, and event types are available for import from agentops module. Module initialization completes without import errors.

metadata.prompt: Import and expose AgentOps core modules: legacy session management (start_session, end_session, track_agent, track_tool, Session, ToolEvent, ErrorEvent, ActionEvent, LLMEvent), modern decorators (trace, session, agent, task, workflow, operation, tool, guardrail, track_endpoint), semantic convention attributes (AgentAttributes, ToolAttributes, WorkflowAttributes, CoreAttributes, SpanAttributes, SpanKind), client (Client), tracing utilities (TraceContext, tracer, get_current_span), enums (TraceState, SUCCESS, ERROR, UNSET, StatusCode), and logging/deprecation helpers. Ensure backward compatibility with legacy API while exposing modern instrumentation decorators.

skill_drafts.name: Semantic Convention Attribute Mapping
skill_drafts.description: Reference schema for mapping agent, tool, workflow, and core execution attributes to OpenTelemetry semantic conventions. Defines standardized attribute names and span kinds for consistent span instrumentation across tracing systems.
skill_drafts.objective: Provide standardized semantic attribute schema for span instrumentation
applicable_signals: Instrumenting agent, tool, workflow, or core operation spans
contraindications: Using non-standard or proprietary attribute naming schemes
When semantic conventions are not required or explicitly disabled
In systems that do not support OpenTelemetry tracing
triggers: Adding attributes to spans, defining span semantics, or ensuring compliance with OpenTelemetry standards
constraints: Attribute names must match OpenTelemetry semantic convention definitions
SpanKind assignment must align with operation type
All four attribute classes (Agent, Tool, Workflow, Core) should be consulted for completeness
output_contract: Consistent, standards-compliant attribute naming across all instrumented spans; all span attributes conform to AgentAttributes, ToolAttributes, WorkflowAttributes, CoreAttributes, and SpanAttributes schemas

metadata.prompt: Use this reference to ensure all instrumented spans employ standardized semantic attribute names from OpenTelemetry conventions. Map execution context (agent state, tool invocation, workflow progress, core operations) to the corresponding AgentAttributes, ToolAttributes, WorkflowAttributes, CoreAttributes, and SpanAttributes classes. Verify span kind assignment (SpanKind) matches the operation type.

skill_drafts.name: Decorator-Based Span Instrumentation
skill_drafts.description: Apply OpenTelemetry decorators to instrument functions and methods with automatic span creation and lifecycle management. Use when adding tracing to agent operations, tool calls, workflows, or endpoints without manual span control.
skill_drafts.objective: Enable declarative span creation and lifecycle management via decorators for agent operations
applicable_signals: Function or method requires distributed tracing
Workflow or task execution must be traced
contraindications: Custom span lifecycle logic is needed
workflow_steps: Import the appropriate decorator from agentops.sdk.decorators
Apply the decorator to the target function or method
Decorator automatically creates and manages the OpenTelemetry span
Span kind and semantic attributes are set based on decorator type
Function executes within the span context
Span lifecycle (start, end, status) is managed automatically
triggers: Adding automatic tracing to agent functions
Desired automatic span lifecycle without manual management
constraints: Decorator must be imported from agentops.sdk.decorators
Target function must be compatible with decorator wrapping
OpenTelemetry context must be initialized before decorator application
cautions: Ensure OpenTelemetry SDK is properly initialized before using decorators
Decorator stacking may create nested spans; verify intended span hierarchy
Exception handling within decorated functions is automatically captured in span status
output_contract: Decorated functions automatically create and manage OpenTelemetry spans with appropriate span kind and attributes. Spans are properly closed and status is recorded upon function completion or exception.

metadata.prompt: Import decorators from agentops.sdk.decorators (@trace, @session, @agent, @task, @workflow, @operation, @tool, @guardrail, @track_endpoint). Apply the appropriate decorator to the target function or method. The decorator automatically creates an OpenTelemetry span, sets the span kind and semantic attributes, and manages the span lifecycle (start, end, status). No manual span creation or closure is required.
